title: Blocking inside async
sub: Wait, Sleep and the Unity context deadlock
cards/0/title: A ticket office with four windows
cards/0/body:
A map tile loader downloads small pieces of a map. To avoid flooding the server, it lets at most four tiles download at once. Think of a ticket office with four windows: the fifth person waits until a window frees up.

In C# this "office" is a SemaphoreSlim(4). You take a spot with Wait and give it back with Release. You are reviewing a method that uses it inside async. It has three problems at once.
cards/1/title: async does not mean "on another thread"
cards/1/body:
An async method runs as plain code on the caller's thread, right up to the first await that has not already finished. Only there does the method step aside and release the thread.

So everything before the first await, including a blocking Wait(), runs on whichever thread called the method. If the method is called from a GetOrAdd factory, the factory runs on that same thread too.
cards/2/q: Game code on the Unity main thread calls GetTileAsync(7, ct). All 4 semaphore spots are taken. Which thread will block in _throttle.Wait()?
cards/2/options/0: The Unity main thread: it made the call
cards/2/options/1: A thread-pool thread: async always moves to the pool
cards/2/options/2: A new thread created by the semaphore
cards/2/explain: Until the first unfinished await, the method runs synchronously on the caller's thread. The GetOrAdd factory is also called synchronously. So Wait() blocks the main thread and the game freezes.
cards/2/wrong/1: async by itself moves nothing to the pool. That is what Task.Run does.
cards/3/title: The deadlock through the Unity context
cards/3/body:
The Unity main thread has its own SynchronizationContext. An await that starts on the main thread captures that context, and the continuation is queued back to the main thread. Unity drains that queue once per frame, in its player loop.

Now the picture: four loads hold the spots, and their continuations (where Release lives) wait for the main thread. The main thread is stuck in Wait(), waiting for a spot to free up. Each waits for the other. That is a deadlock.
cards/3/deep: The context is captured only if SynchronizationContext.Current is not null where the await runs. In Unity that is the main thread. If the four loads holding the spots started on a pool thread, their continuations run in the pool, Release happens, and the main thread only stalls until a spot frees up. That is why the bug comes and goes: it depends on which thread started the loads that hold the spots.
cards/4/q: Put the deadlock steps in order.
cards/4/items/0: Four loads take all semaphore spots and wait for the network
cards/4/items/1: The main thread calls GetTileAsync and blocks in Wait(): no spots left
cards/4/items/2: A network reply arrives; the continuation (with Release) is queued to the main thread
cards/4/items/3: The main thread never drains its queue: it is blocked in Wait()
cards/4/items/4: Release never runs, no spot is freed, Wait never wakes up
cards/4/explain: A closed loop: the main thread waits for Release, and only the main thread can run Release.
cards/5/task: Find three problems: a blocked thread, a spot that may never be released, and a needless thread stall. Tap the lines, then press Check.
cards/5/bugs/0/title: Synchronous Wait() in an async method
cards/5/bugs/0/why: It blocks the calling thread. On the Unity main thread that freezes the game and deadlocks: the continuations that call Release are waiting for this very thread.
cards/5/bugs/1/why: It blocks the whole thread. The continuation after await came back to the Unity main thread, so the frame stalls for 50 ms per tile. Use await Task.Delay(50, ct): it holds no thread.
cards/5/bugs/2/why: If the network or Parse throws, the code never reaches Release. After four such errors all spots are lost for good and every load hangs.
cards/6/body:
Picture a cloakroom with 4 hooks. A person hangs a coat, trips on the way out and never comes back. That hook is taken forever. After four such people the cloakroom is closed to everyone.

That is Release without finally. One network error and a spot is gone. _pending is not decremented either, so _allLoaded never fires. A single failure shuts down the whole loader, and with no message in the log: loads just "hang".
cards/6/deep: One detail when fixing it: open the try after the spot is acquired. If WaitAsync(ct) throws OperationCanceledException (cancellation), the finally must not call Release: you never took a spot, and the semaphore count would grow above the original 4.
cards/7/q: The loader has no try/finally. Four loads in a row fail (the server returns errors). What happens to a fifth, perfectly healthy load?
cards/7/options/0: It hangs waiting for a spot: all 4 spots are lost
cards/7/options/1: It works; the semaphore recovers by itself
cards/7/explain: A semaphore only remembers how many spots are free. A load that failed never returned its spot, and the semaphore does not know. After four losses there are zero free spots, permanently.
cards/7/wrong/1: SemaphoreSlim does not track who took what. It cannot recover on its own.
cards/8/q: Build the correct "ticket office": it waits without blocking and returns the spot in every case.
cards/8/explain: WaitAsync holds no thread and Task.Delay does not block one. finally runs on success and on error, and the Release inside it returns the spot.
cards/9/q: What is true about ConfigureAwait(false) in this loader?
cards/9/options/0: The continuation after await usually runs on the thread pool, not the Unity main thread
cards/9/options/1: The heavy Tile.Parse then no longer slows down frames
cards/9/options/2: Right after it you can safely touch Unity scene objects
cards/9/options/3: By itself it removes the blocking Wait()
cards/9/explain: ConfigureAwait(false) means "do not return to the captured context", so parsing leaves the main thread. You must not touch Unity API after it. It does not remove Wait(), which runs before the first await. It does break the deadlock loop, though: Release runs on the pool and wakes the main thread, although the game still freezes until then.
cards/10/q: Match the symptom to its cause.
cards/10/pairs/0/0: A frame hitches after every downloaded tile
cards/10/pairs/0/1: Thread.Sleep in a continuation on the main thread
cards/10/pairs/1/0: After a few network errors no tiles load at all
cards/10/pairs/2/0: The game hangs forever while the CPU sits idle
cards/10/pairs/2/1: Deadlock: the continuation with Release waits for the blocked main thread
cards/10/pairs/3/0: The deadlock is gone after ConfigureAwait(false), but the game still stalls at times
cards/10/pairs/3/1: Wait() before the first await still blocks the main thread
